questions.question: What risks do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each tie to the responsible use and regulation of AI in their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says concerns about the responsible use of AI in its products and services may cause reputational or financial harm and liability, and may lead it to incur costs to resolve such issues [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It says AI solutions with unintended consequences, copyright or publicity-rights infringement, or controversial effects on human rights, privacy or employment could bring brand harm, competitive harm or legal liability [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. NVIDIA also says complying with multiple AI regulations across jurisdictions may raise its cost of doing business and could impede its ability to offer certain products in some jurisdictions [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It cites the European Union, where regulation tied to the EU Code of Practice for General Purpose AI could require it to notify the European Commission about some Trustworthy AI processes [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. NVIDIA adds that the EU AI Act may affect its ability to train, deploy or release AI models in the EU, and that new state laws effective January 1, 2026 may do the same and raise compliance costs [0001045810-26-000021:0039]. It also says regulatory restrictions targeting products that enable AI, including export controls on GPUs and related products, could limit its ability to export and put it at a competitive disadvantage [0001045810-26-000021:0040].
AMD says issues related to the responsible use of AI may result in reputational, competitive and financial harm and liability [0000002488-26-000018:0052]. It cites third-party misuse of AI, and inadequate AI development or deployment practices by AMD or its customers, as things that could harm society and impair public acceptance of AI [0000002488-26-000018:0052]. AMD says new and proposed AI legislation could cause greater compliance costs, affect the ability of its customers to acquire and use systems with its AI-related products, and reduce the number of customers [0000002488-26-000018:0052]. It notes the EU AI Act, adopted in 2024 and phased in over the next few years, and says such laws may impede its ability to offer certain products and services in certain jurisdictions if it cannot comply [0000002488-26-000018:0051]. questions.question: What forms of long-term supply commitment do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-K risk factors, and what happens to each if demand falls short?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says that to secure future supply and capacity it has paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased its product costs [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It also says it has entered into prepaid manufacturing and capacity agreements for current and future products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. If demand falls short, NVIDIA says it may be unable to use on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments accordingly [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It says it has had to reduce average selling prices, write down inventory, incur cancellation penalties and record impairments, and may have to do so again [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It adds that non-cancellable and non-returnable purchase orders amplify these risks [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It also says it may incur inventory provisions or impairments if its inventory or its supply or capacity commitments exceed demand [0001045810-26-000021:0023].
AMD says it has long-term purchase commitments and prepayment arrangements with some of its suppliers [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. If AMD overestimates demand or demand decreases, it says the result could be excess inventory and an increase in production costs, particularly because of its prepayment arrangements with certain suppliers [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. AMD is also party to a wafer supply agreement with GF, under which GF provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026 [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. If AMD's actual wafer requirements are below the applicable annual wafer purchase target, it could have excess inventory or higher inventory unit costs, which may hurt its gross margin and results of operations [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
Intel says it has entered into arrangements with some suppliers that involve long-term purchase commitments and/or large prepayments, to obtain certain materials and components (particularly substrates) and third-party foundry manufacturing capacity [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. If future customer demand over the horizon of these arrangements falls below its expectations, Intel says it could have excess or obsolete inventory, unneeded capacity and increased costs [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. It adds that its prepayments may not be fully utilized, and in some cases may not be fully recoverable [0000050863-26-000011:0075].

Gaming revenue rose 41% on strong Blackwell demand [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. questions.question: How was Intel's sale of a majority stake in Altera structured, and how did it affect Intel's FY2025 financial statements?

answer.text:
Structure of the sale: On April 14, 2025, Intel signed a transaction agreement with SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of SLP, to sell 51% of the issued and outstanding common stock of Altera, its wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The sale closed on September 12, 2025, for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. That figure consisted of $4.3 billion in cash proceeds at closing, $500 million in deferred cash proceeds received in the third quarter of 2025, and $500 million in deferred cash proceeds payable no later than December 31, 2027 [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It was offset by $400 million of cash transferred to Altera, approximately $469 million of separation and employee-related costs Intel agreed to fund to SLP, and other direct and incremental costs of the sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel retained a 49% minority investment in Altera, which is accounted for under the equity method [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
It therefore deconsolidated Altera on September 12, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
- The carrying amounts of Altera's net assets sold at closing included total assets of $2,762 million and total liabilities of $400 million [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
It is classified within equity investments on the Consolidated Balance Sheets at December 27, 2025, and was recognized as a non-cash investing activity [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
- The carrying value of the investment was $3.2 billion at December 27, 2025, and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
- Intel recognized a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion within interest and other, net in 2025 (calculated as $5,553 million) [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
- About $2.1 billion of the gain resulted from remeasuring the retained investment to fair value at the closing date [0000050863-26-000011:0147].
They are presented in net cash provided by (used for) investing activities [0000050863-26-000011:0147].
It also had $327 million within other accrued liabilities and $97 million within other long-term liabilities for amounts payable to SLP for separation and employee-related costs [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
It was partially offset by a $1.8 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the Escrowed Shares and by $229 million of charges related to the NAND memory business sale [0000050863-26-000011:0046].
- Intel's effective tax rate rose in 2025, offset in part by the nonrecurring 2025 gain on the Altera divestiture [0000050863-26-000011:0046].
- Intel is still finalizing customary closing adjustments with SLP, which could change the final net cash proceeds and the gain on sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
- Intel provides wafer manufacturing services to Altera, a related party, and will be reimbursed for costs incurred on Altera's behalf under a transition services agreement [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

questions.question: What did Intel's FY2024 10-K say about its policy on dividends and stock repurchases, and what constrains its ability to return cash to stockholders?

answer.text:
Intel said it has ceased to return capital to stockholders: in recent years it has not made stock repurchases, and it reduced and then suspended its quarterly dividend in the fourth quarter of 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Its last share repurchase under its authorization occurred in Q1 2021, and no shares were repurchased during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0083][0000050863-25-000009:0084]. As of December 28, 2024, Intel was authorized to repurchase up to $110.0 billion, of which $7.2 billion remained available [0000050863-25-000009:0083][0000050863-25-000009:0084]. Intel is not obligated to make repurchases under the program, and it gave no assurance about the amount, timing or execution of future repurchases or that any repurchases would enhance long-term stockholder value [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Shares withheld for tax purposes on RSU vesting are treated as common stock repurchases in the Consolidated Financial Statements but are not counted as repurchases under the authorized program [0000050863-25-000009:0084].
The filing names one explicit constraint on dividends: under its commercial CHIPS Act agreement, Intel agreed to forgo paying dividends for the next two years and to limits on dividend payments for the three years after that [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Intel also said there can be no assurance that it will be able to pay dividends in the future [0000050863-25-000009:0073].
It had $51.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes and other borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024, and it said its debt level and debt service obligations could reduce its flexibility [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. It also reported a net loss attributable to Intel of $18,756 million for FY2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0092]. Its funding requirements include capital expenditures, with commitments of $14.0 billion for 2025 and $6.0 billion in the long term [0000050863-25-000009:0042].

Intel's FY2025 10-K describes the U.S. government equity transactions, including the equity issuances and the amendment to the commercial CHIPS Act agreement, as complex and subject to a number of risks and uncertainties [0000050863-26-000011:0069].

The 10-K lists these risks:

- The legislative, judicial or executive branches of the U.S. government could determine in the future that all or part of the transactions were unauthorized, void or voidable. Only the Department of Commerce is contractually bound, and no other agency or branch has committed to support or refrain from challenging the transaction [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- Legal challenges, administrative rulings, litigation or geopolitical developments could materially impair funding, alter obligations under the CHIPS Act agreements, or otherwise adversely affect the transactions. Enforcement against a government counterparty is also inherently uncertain given the defenses available to the U.S. government [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- The transactions eliminate Intel's contractual rights to receive future grant funds under the commercial CHIPS Act agreement and the Secure Enclave agreement, and may limit its ability to secure grants from government entities in the future. Intel will no longer benefit from the reduced future operating costs that such grant funding would have made possible [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- It is uncertain whether other government entities may seek to convert their existing grant arrangements into equity investments or be unwilling to support Intel with future grants. Either outcome could limit access to capital, increase the cost of capital or increase future operating costs [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- The transactions are dilutive to existing stockholders, because shares were issued to the U.S. government at a discount to the current market price. Stockholders may suffer significant additional dilution if the conditions to the warrant are triggered and the warrant is exercised [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- The government's equity position reduces the voting and other governance rights of other stockholders. The U.S. government became one of Intel's largest stockholders, and its interests may differ from those of other stockholders [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- The U.S. government has agreed to vote its shares as recommended by Intel's board, subject to applicable law and exceptions that protect its interests. This will reduce the voting influence of other stockholders on director selection and stockholder proposals [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- The significant government stake and the government's substantial additional powers over laws and regulations affecting Intel may substantially limit its ability to pursue future strategic transactions that could benefit stockholders. It may also make third parties less willing to engage in such transactions with Intel [0000050863-26-000011:0069].
- Intel's non-U.S. business may be adversely affected. Sales outside the U.S. were 70% of its 2025 revenue, and having the U.S. government as a significant stockholder could subject Intel to additional regulations, obligations or restrictions in other countries, such as foreign subsidy laws [0000050863-26-000011:0070].

Intel states that any of these risks could have a material adverse effect on its revenue, operations, financial position, cash flows, access to financing, cost structure, competitiveness, reputation, profitability and prospects, and could exacerbate other risks discussed in the 10-K [0000050863-26-000011:0070].

If it could not secure and maintain enough capacity on favorable pricing terms, it might be unable to make its products in sufficient volume and at a cost that supports its products business [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Only TSMC and Samsung can currently produce the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes Intel's products need [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If competitors were more successful in securing capacity with those foundries, Intel's product roadmap, market position and customer relationships would be materially adversely impacted [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

questions.question: What is the status of the third Texas patent case and the related license defense in Intel's VLSI litigation, according to the FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022 with one remaining VLSI patent, and the jury found the patent valid and infringed and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. The court has not yet entered final judgment, and Intel filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law in February 2023 [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
On the license defense, Intel moved in April 2024 to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted that motion the same month [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In May 2025 the court held a trial on an underlying factual question relating to the license defense, and the jury returned a verdict in Intel's favor [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. questions.question: How much did AMD spend repurchasing shares under its stock repurchase program in 2025 compared with 2024, and how did the amount remaining available under the program change?

answer.text:
In 2025, AMD spent $1.3 billion repurchasing 12.4 million shares of common stock under its stock repurchase program [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. In 2024, it spent $862 million repurchasing 5.9 million shares under the program [0000002488-25-000012:0070]. The 2025 figure therefore exceeded the 2024 figure by roughly $0.4 billion, based on the stated amounts [0000002488-26-000018:0071][0000002488-25-000012:0070].
The amount remaining available rose from $4.7 billion as of December 28, 2024 [0000002488-25-000012:0070] to $9.4 billion as of December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. The increase came even though AMD repurchased shares during 2025, because on May 13, 2025 the board approved a new $6 billion repurchase program that was added to the existing program and increased the total repurchase authority to $14 billion [0000002488-25-000166:0024]. The program was previously authorized for up to $12 billion [0000002488-25-000012:0112]. No shares were repurchased during the three months ended December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0068].
